purpose: resolve whether the previous zero-pruning K3 affine result was caused mainly by dropping nonnegativity, before introducing any active-transition tangent/secant approximation
scientific_question: does the exact convex hull of static K3 candidate endpoints for each fixed final-stage class conservatively eliminate any wrong final stages on the already-spent ABCD Pythia-14M target?
target_selection: already-spent fixed ABCD target used by prior K3, inverse, forward-reachable, and affine diagnostics
static_k3_candidate_class: for final stage j, the six degree-three truncated endpoint predictions whose complete A/B/C/D chronology ends in j
fixed_last_n4_equivalence: for N=4 and K=3, imposing nonnegative local-order marginals plus candidate-last constraints reduces exactly to the simplex convex hull of the six static K3 candidate endpoints ending in that stage; this diagnostic therefore isolates the effect of restoring nonnegativity relative to the prior affine hull
candidate_vertices_source: algebraic K3 predictions from the frozen 40-execution ordered-interaction basis; no candidate training replay
diagnostic_scalability_scope: the N=4 six-vertex active-set implementation is a confound resolver only and is not itself claimed as a general subfactorial decoder
primary_feasible_upper_bound_source: frozen K3 nearest history for the same spent ABCD target
certificate_definition: for a candidate class C_j=conv{q_i}, choose any unit vector u and define L_j=min_i <u,y-q_i>; then dist(y,C_j)>=L_j by Cauchy-Schwarz and linearity over a convex hull. The projection solver is used only to propose u=(y-p)/||y-p||; the reported elimination certificate is the independently recomputed dual witness L_j, not the numerical primal distance.
elimination_rule: candidate last stage j is certified impossible for the static K3 nearest-history problem only if its independently recomputed dual witness lower bound exceeds primary_feasible_upper_bound_error + numerical_lower_bound_guard
required_sanity_checks: target endpoint hash exactly replays ABCD
frozen BACD feasible upper-bound error reproduces within tolerance
all candidate convex weights are primal feasible within tolerance
each dual witness vector is unit norm within tolerance when the candidate hull distance is nonzero
each dual witness lower bound is no larger than the independently recomputed primal convex-hull distance beyond tolerance
each primal convex-hull distance is no larger than the minimum vertex error beyond tolerance
strong_success_requires: A, B, and C are all certified impossible while D survives
promising_partial_requires: at least one of A/B/C is certified impossible while D survives
scientific_negative_requires: zero of A/B/C is certified impossible while D survives and every sanity check passes
invalid_run_requires: D is eliminated, a frozen replay/hash check fails, or any primal/dual certificate sanity inequality fails
interpretation_scope: this diagnostic certifies only candidate classes inside the static degree-three truncated endpoint model. It cannot certify the true ABCD chronology because the N=4 K3 truncation omits degree-four interaction structure.
next_step_if_strong_success: treat the previous affine failure as primarily a relaxation-looseness result; build a generic nonnegative K-local marginal dual bound and test certified branch-and-bound/ambiguity on spent synthetic and model data before adding active-transition approximations
next_step_if_partial: retain nonnegative K-local convex bounds as the first pruning layer, then test an interaction-order lift or active-transition-preserving refinement only on the surviving ambiguity set
next_step_if_scientific_negative: the nonnegativity confound is resolved against static K3; prioritize an interaction-order lift that compiles exact candidate transitions into degree K+1 interactions, with an explicit omitted-higher-order tail bound before any true-chronology certificate
launch_blockers: add deterministic synthetic tests proving the dual witness is always a lower bound, including deliberately inexact projection directions
